subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: Should this broad VPS reasoning-latency investigation be accepted as a public runbook/instrumentation effort, and what measurement environment plus acceptance criteria define done?
rationale: The issue is valid and aligned with performance priorities, but static repository review cannot choose the benchmark host, trace format, measurement depth, or how much analysis belongs in docs versus code without maintainer intent.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Define one native-Linux Gateway measurement path and use existing telemetry before approving targeted instrumentation or optimization PRs.

options.title: Split into narrow diagnostics issues
options.body: Close or pause the broad umbrella only after creating separate issues for context assembly, memory search, compaction, Telegram delivery, and subagent timing gaps.

options.title: Treat as support-only
options.body: Keep product docs unchanged and direct future reporter-specific performance analysis to support unless a reproducible core bottleneck appears.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Define one native-Linux Gateway measurement path and use existing telemetry before approving targeted instrumentation or optimization PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame routes the most relevant docs and embedded-run diagnostic surfaces through vincentkoc, making him the clearest routing owner for the scoping decision.
